title: FDCA: Fine-grained Digital-CIM based CNN Accelerator with Hybrid Quantization and Weight-Stationary Dataflow
problem: Fine-grained digital-CIM operations for CNN acceleration suffer from parasitic effects on word and bit lines, and approximation-induced errors that degrade efficiency and accuracy without systematic mitigation.
motivation: Fine-grained DCIMs offer significant energy and area efficiency potential for CNNs, but their benefits have remained largely unexplored due to unaddressed challenges in managing parasitic effects and maintaining precision.
method: FDCA reduces precision and circuit complexity through hybrid quantization guided by hessian trace (a mathematical measure of which parameters matter most) and approximation schemes that balance computation speed against storage time. It generates approximate shift-and-accumulate circuits (simplified arithmetic operations) using Cartesian Genetic Programming (an algorithm that evolves optimal circuit designs), then pairs them with error-compensating adder trees that correct for the approximation errors. Finally, it uses weight-stationary dataflow (keeping weights fixed in place while input activations flow through the hardware) to maximize digital-CIM utilization and eliminate idle computation cycles.
key_novelty: FDCA's core advance is combining hessian-based hybrid quantization with Cartesian Genetic Programming-designed approximate arithmetic specifically optimized for fine-grained digital-CIM operations.
contributions: Hybrid quantization leveraging hessian trace and computation/storage time ratio to balance accuracy and efficiency
Cartesian Genetic Programming based approximate shift-and-accumulate with error compensation for fine-grained DCIM
Optimized weight-stationary dataflow improving CIM utilization and eliminating dataflow stalls
primary_theme: Energy-efficient CNN acceleration via fine-grained digital-CIM with hybrid quantization
